Order No. 04/Dated 11th September, 2024 1.
Heard learned counsel for the appellants.

2. The learned Single Judge has dismissed the writ petition on the ground that the land has been recorded in the name of Gairmajarua Malik in the revisional survey conducted sometime in the year 2005.

3. It appears from the Rehabilitation and Resettlement Policy of Coal India Ltd., 2012 that the "land owner" and "displaced person" have been defined under Clause 4(c) and 4(d) respectively, for ready reference, Clause 4(c) and 4(d) are being referred hereunder as :-
"4.(c) "land owner" includes any person- (i) whose name is recorded as the owner of the land or part thereof, in the records of the concerned authority; or (ii) who is entitled to be granted Patta rights on the land under any law of the State including assigned lands; or (iii) who has been declared as such by an order of the court or District Collector.
4.(d) Displaced person - means and includes any person who is deprived of his homestead on account of acquisition Provided that the person/family who does not ordinarily reside in the Saraswati Devi vs The State Of Jharkhand on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106437845/

4. It is evident from the aforesaid provision the "land owner" can be construed to be a land owner if any person whose name is recorded as the owner of the land or part thereof, in the records of the concerned authority or who is entitled to be granted Patta rights on the land under any law of the State including assigned lands, or who has been declared as such by an order of the court or District Collector.
5. The "displaced person" means and includes any person who is deprived of his homestead on account of acquisition.

Provided that the person/family who does not ordinarily reside in the homestead land acquired for the project can be termed "Displaced" but he will be eligible for compensation only for homestead and not for livelihood.

6. It is evident from Page 126-127 of the paper book that the Circle Officer has admitted the possession of the appellants/writ petitioners over the land in question and, hence, the status of the appellants, as per the definition of "displaced person" will be of "displaced person" and in that view of the matter, as per the Rehabilitation and Resettlement Policy of Coal India Ltd., 2012, the appellants are to be held to be entitled for compensation.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 7. The State is to respond that if the revenue authority has admitted by giving a report about the possession of the writ petitioners/appellants, then why the appellants will not be held entitled for the compensation.

8. This Court, has posed a pinpointed question upon Mr. Mohan Kumar Dubey, learned A.C. to Advocate General that on what basis the claim of the writ petitioner is being disputed so far as the compensation is concerned when as per the report of the Circle Officer, Balumath, the update rent receipts have been issued.

9. The response has been given by referring to paragraph 8 of the counter affidavit filed by the Sub- Divisional Officer, before the learned writ court wherein even the claim of the petitioner with respect to the possession over the land in question has been disputed.

10. This Court has posed further question upon the learned State counsel that on what basis the Sub-Divisional Officer has disputed the possession when the revenue authority who has got competence under the Bihar Tenants' Holdings (Maintenance of Records) Act, 1973 has given a report on issuance of rent receipt.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 11. The learned State Counsel is not in a position to answer the same.

12. This Court, therefore, is of the view that let the Sub- Divisional Officer, who has sworn the affidavit, appear in person along with the explanation that on what basis such statement has been made at paragraph-8 of the counter affidavit.

14. It is clarified that learned State counsel is to state on oath that who was the Circle Officer at the time when the report was submitted and who was the Sub-Divisional Officer who has filed the affidavit.

15. Let Sub-Divisional Officer who has filed the affidavit along with the present incumbent in the office and the Circle Officer who had submitted the report along with present incumbent, appear physically in Court on 18.09.2024 along with the revenue records.
16. This Court is of the view that before passing any adverse order against the erring officials,
